title: Generalized Pain
diagnosis: Sickle Cell Anemia with Acute Chest Syndrome and Pneumonia
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a 6-year-old boy with previously undiagnosed sickle cell disease (HbSS) who presents with generalized body pain, fever, and respiratory distress consistent with acute vaso-occlusive crisis complicated by acute chest syndrome and lobar pneumonia (H. influenzae B). CBC shows anemia. Peripheral smear demonstrates sickled cells. Hemoglobin electrophoresis is REQUIRED for definitive diagnosis — it differentiates HbSS from other thalassemias. Sickle cell disease is autosomal recessive: single amino acid substitution (valine for glutamic acid) on beta-globin chain → HbS. Does not present before 6 months due to protective HbF. Patients are functionally asplenic by age 8 from repeated splenic infarction → susceptible to encapsulated organisms (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae B, Salmonella). Management: IV fluids (dehydration precipitates sickling), IV opioids (morphine) for severe pain, oxygen for hypoxia, IV ceftriaxone (CAP treatment), blood transfusion if acute chest syndrome with hypoxia unresponsive to O2. Hydroxyurea stimulates HbF production. Penicillin prophylaxis (lifelong if severe infection history). Consult pediatric hematology. Admit to inpatient. Meningococcal vaccine early (asplenia risk).
chief_complaint: Generalized pain, fever, respiratory distress, fatigue

stacks.label: Peripheral smear, blood
stacks.finding: Shows sickled cells. Hb electrophoresis is REQUIRED — smear alone insufficient for definitive diagnosis.

stacks.label: Hemoglobin electrophoresis
stacks.finding: REQUIRED for diagnosis. Differentiates HbSS from thalassemias and other hemoglobinopathies. HbS confirmed.

stacks.label: Chest X-ray
stacks.finding: Sickle cell patients prone to infection — screen. May show infiltrates (pneumonia/ACS).

stacks.label: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: ACS vs pulmonary infection — oxygenation guides management.

stacks.label: Urinalysis
stacks.finding: Fever + pain — UA for GU source.

stacks.label: Bacterial culture, blood
stacks.finding: SIRS criteria met — blood cultures before antibiotics.

stacks.label: PT/PTT / INR
stacks.finding: Low Hb — rule out coagulopathy as cause.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP / LFTs
stacks.finding: Screening.

stacks.label: Oxygen
stacks.finding: Low SpO2 — supplemental O2.

stacks.label: IV fluids (NS / LR / D5NS / D5½NS)
stacks.finding: Dehydration precipitates sickling — IV fluids promptly.

stacks.label: IV opioids (Morphine / Fentanyl / Hydromorphone)
stacks.finding: Sickle cell crisis is incredibly painful — pain medication is essential.

stacks.label: Type and screen
stacks.finding: Will likely need transfusion — type and screen pre-emptively.

stacks.label: Hydroxyurea
stacks.finding: Stimulates fetal hemoglobin (HbF) production — improves symptoms long-term.

stacks.label: IV Ceftriaxone / Cefotaxime (CAP treatment)
stacks.finding: Community-acquired pneumonia — IV cephalosporin. Blood culture shows H. influenzae B.

stacks.label: Folic acid
stacks.finding: Supports erythropoiesis — standard in sickle cell disease.

stacks.label: Penicillin V prophylaxis
stacks.finding: Penicillin prophylaxis for encapsulated organisms. Lifelong if history of severe infection (H. influenzae). Debate about stopping at age 5 without infection history.

stacks.label: Consult, pediatric hematology/oncology
stacks.finding: New diagnosis — hematology for disease education and ongoing management.

stacks.label: PRBC transfusion / Exchange transfusion
stacks.finding: ACS with hypoxia unresponsive to O2 — transfusion to dilute HbS. Goal HbS <30%.

stacks.label: IV access
stacks.finding: Good practice.

stacks.label: Medication compliance counseling
stacks.finding: Essential to prevent future crises.

stacks.label: Meningococcal vaccine
stacks.finding: Functional asplenia → vulnerable to encapsulated organisms. Give early (normally age 11-12).

physical_exam.respiratory: Dyspneic — acute chest syndrome with pneumonia.
physical_exam.skin: Pallor from anemia. Dactylitis possible (hand-foot syndrome).

decoys.label: Hemoglobin electrophoresis not ordered (smear only)
decoys.reason_wrong: Peripheral smear suggestive but NOT definitive. Hb electrophoresis is REQUIRED to differentiate HbSS from thalassemias and other hemoglobinopathies. Points deducted if not done.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Gold standard for sickle cell disease. Differentiates HbSS from sickle cell trait, HbSC, thalassemias. Peripheral smear is suggestive but insufficient.

teach_me_steps.order: IV fluids + IV opioids + O2 for vaso-occlusive crisis
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Hydration prevents sickling. Opioids for severe pain. O2 for hypoxia. Blood cultures then empiric antibiotics.
Hydroxyurea → ↑ HbF. Penicillin for encapsulated organisms (functional asplenia). Meningococcal vaccine early.

case_summary: New diagnosis sickle cell disease (HbSS) at age 6. Vaso-occlusive crisis + acute chest syndrome + H. influenzae pneumonia. IVF + morphine + O2 + IV ceftriaxone + hydroxyurea + penicillin. Transfusion for ACS. Admit.
